newsitem.title: ZAIRE: France will evacuate other nationals from Zaire - army.
newsitem.headline: France will evacuate other nationals from Zaire - army.

text.p: French troops are preparing to evacuate not only French citizens but other threatened nationals if civil war reaches the Zaire capital, a French army commander said on Tuesday.

General Rene Landrin, commander of the 300-strong French force standing by in neighbouring Congo, told Radio France Internationale that the principal task of his troops was to evacuate French nationals.
"But there is no exclusion," he added. "The French will not say you are Senegalese, you are Ivorian, you stay."

In what could be a massive operation far surpassing the U.S. military's evacuation of foreigners from Liberia in April and May 1995, Landrin said the French would help "all countries that have citizens on Zairean soil".
France, the United States, Belgium and Britain have separately stationed a total of more than 1,000 troops in the Congo capital Brazzaville across the Zaire River from Kinshasa.
They have stepped up manoeuvres, notably on the river, simulating evacuation, amid heightened threats of attack soon by rebels who have seized half the vast country.

The government has publicly dismissed rebel claims that they will march on Kinshasa in about three weeks to topple President Mobutu Sese Seko. But authorities say government army units are now patrolling districts of the city, on the lookout for the slightest sign of guerrillas.

Emergency rule Prime Minister Likulia Bolongo vowed on state television on Monday night that the beleaguered army would never surrender the capital to rebels and called on residents to be prepared for resistance.
"The army is prepared to defend Kinshasa," Likulia said. "All dispositions have been taken to defend Kinshasa. I can assure you that we have sufficient arms to assure the security of the capital."
But the government will have to work much harder to reassure a population all too aware of the army's inability to resist the rebels elsewhere and its penchant for looting before fleeing.
Kinshasa is the most important city still outside the hands of the rebels, who launched their guerrilla campaign from Zaire's eastern provinces last October.
